dismissed.why_not_material: Claim about sBA biomarker association is not about the catalyst trial (MARCH-PFIC, NCT03905330) but about the INDIGO trial in Alagille syndrome, a different indication. The claim text explicitly states 'INDIGO: sBA Response Associated with Transplant-Free Survival' – INDIGO is the separate Alagille program, not the PFIC catalyst.
Claim about sBA response association is from the same INDIGO (Alagille syndrome) presentation/data as mirm_023, not the MARCH-PFIC catalyst trial. Different program, different indication.

Claim references a six-year natural history comparison for LIVMARLI in Alagille syndrome (ALGS), not the PFIC catalyst trial. Cross-trial benchmark claims about a different indication do not bear on whether the PFIC Phase 3 readout is masked.

Explicitly references event-free survival data 'in patients with Alagille syndrome' from a natural history comparison. Different indication from the PFIC catalyst; not material to MARCH-PFIC readout masking.

While dated 2022-01-11 and discussing PFIC Phase 3, the claim about '6-year analysis...vs natural history control from GALA database' references the INDIGO trial in PFIC2 specifically (as noted in finding context), which appears to be open-label extension or earlier data, not the blinded catalyst trial NCT03905330. This is supporting color from earlier-phase work, consistent with principle #3.

References INDIGO trial vs natural history cohort for PFIC2. This appears to be open-label or earlier-phase supportive data alongside the pivotal, not a misrepresentation of the catalyst trial's basis. Standard biotech promotion per principle #3.
Six-year event-free survival data presented at AASLD is for Alagille syndrome (ALGS context from other claims), not the PFIC catalyst trial. Different indication.

Timeline guidance of Q4 2022 vs registered Q3 2022 primary completion is a minor discrepancy. Given the registry shows completion_slipped=True for this trial, modest timeline drift is expected operational noise, not material masking of a likely miss.
Same as mirm_007: Q4 2022 guidance vs Q3 2022 registered completion. Minor operational timeline variance on a trial with documented slippage; not a tell of data masking.

H2 2022 guidance is consistent with the registered July 2022 completion date (both H2). The finding notes repeated slippage history but the specific guidance here is not inconsistent with the registered date at time of filing.
Same as mirm_016: H2 2022 guidance aligns with July 2022 registered completion. Timeline slippage history is operational noise, not masking of catalyst trial results.

Q2 2022 guidance filed November 2021 when registered completion had already passed (October 2021 per version 22) or was about to slip to Q3 2022. This is operational timeline management on a complex trial; minor severity and no indication of data masking.

Q2 2022 guidance vs registered late-2021 completion shows timeline drift, but this is operational management of a trial with documented slippage. Minor severity; not material to whether the catalyst data is being masked.
Claim states trial is 'Enrolling' in January 2022 when it stopped recruiting shortly after. This is a stale status claim, minor severity, and does not indicate masking of clinical efficacy results.

analyst_note: All 14 refuted findings are dismissed as non-material to the MARCH-PFIC Phase 3 catalyst. The moderate-severity biomarker overreach claims (mirm_023, mirm_024) and several cross-trial comparison claims reference the INDIGO trial in Alagille syndrome, a different indication from the PFIC catalyst. Other cross-trial claims appear to reference open-label extension or earlier PFIC data presented as supportive color alongside the pivotal, which is standard IR practice. The remaining operational timeline findings (all minor severity) reflect modest guidance drift on a trial with documented slippage—expected noise, not data masking. No company-level honesty issues are present, and no material catalyst-trial-specific masking is detected. This is consistent with an honest readout attempt.
